title: The Secret Underground Network of Trees
hook: How does a dying tree pump remaining sugar to a neighboring sapling?
script: How does a dying tree pump remaining sugar to a neighboring sapling? Beneath the silent forest floor, fungi link tree roots into a living underground network. A single teaspoon of dirt holds over thirty feet of these microscopic threads. When insects attack a leaf, chemical warning signals pulse through the soil to alert nearby trees. Some trees even pump toxic compounds through the threads to kill competing seedlings. Before dying, a mature tree sends forty percent of its carbon to young saplings. You are never looking at individual trees, but one living organism.
